405:\begin{theorem}[Rank-independent radial locations for elementary two-groups]
406:\label{thm:elementary-two-group-finite-sampling}
407:Let \(E=(C_2)^r\), with \(r\ge0\).  Let
408:\(\tau:E(\Gamma)\to E\) and \(\tau':E(\Gamma')\to E\) be one-step
409:cocycles over primitive non-negative integral base matrices \(A,A'\), whose
410:sizes are at most \(V\) and whose Perron roots \(\lambda,\lambda'>1\) need
411:not agree.  Put
412:\[
413: x=\min\{\lambda^{-1},(\lambda')^{-1}\},
414: \qquad M(V)=2V\lceil\log_2(4V)\rceil.
415:\]
416:For \(g\in E\), define
417:\[
418: \mathcal E_g^\tau(y)=\sum_{n\ge1}p_{n,g}(\tau)\log(1-y^n),
419: \qquad 0<y<x,
420:\]
421:and define \(\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}\) analogously.  Suppose that
422:\[
423: \mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)=\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)
424: \qquad(g\in E,\ 1\le i\le M(V))
425:\]
426:at \(M(V)\) distinct radii in \((0,x)\), at least one of which is
427:algebraic.  Then
428:\[
429: p_{n,g}(\tau)=p_{n,g}(\tau')
430: \qquad(n\ge1,\ g\in E).
431:\]
432:One radial observation here means the full vector
433:\((\mathcal E_g(y_i))_{g\in E}\).  Thus the theorem uses \(M(V)\)
434:radial locations independently of \(r\), while the total number of scalar
435:equalities assumed is \(|E|M(V)=2^rM(V)\).  Neither a common base
436:presentation nor a strict spectral gap for the non-trivial character blocks
437:is required.
438:\end{theorem}
439:
440:\begin{proof}
441:Absolute convergence follows for each system from the periodic-point estimate
442:used in \Cref{thm:finite-radial-sampling}.  Summing the assumed identities over
443:\(g\in E\) gives, at every sampled radius,
444:\[
445: \log\det(I-y_iA)=\sum_{g\in E}\mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)
446: =\sum_{g\in E}\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)
447: =\log\det(I-y_iA').
448:\]
449:Both determinants are positive on \((0,x)\).  Their difference has degree at
450:most \(V\), vanishes at the \(M(V)\ge V\) distinct non-zero sample points,
451:and also vanishes at zero.  Hence
452:\begin{equation}\label{eq:elementary-two-group-base-determinant-equality}
453: \det(I-zA)=\det(I-zA').
454:\end{equation}
455:
456:Every \(\chi\in\widehat E\) takes values in \(\{\pm1\}\).  Let
457:\(B_{\chi,\tau}\) and \(B_{\chi,\tau'}\) be the corresponding character
458:blocks and put
459:\[
460: H_\chi(z)=\frac{\det(I-zB_{\chi,\tau})}
461:                  {\det(I-zB_{\chi,\tau'})}.
462:\]
463:Since \(\chi(g)\equiv1\pmod2\), entrywise reduction gives
464:\[
465: B_{\chi,\tau}\equiv A\pmod2,
466: \qquad B_{\chi,\tau'}\equiv A'\pmod2.
467:\]
468:Together with \eqref{eq:elementary-two-group-base-determinant-equality}, this
469:shows that the two character determinants are congruent modulo two and hence
470:supports the integral refinement in
471:\Cref{lem:critical-mahler-integrality}; the two blocks need not have the same
472:size.  This congruence is not an input to the parity-free lifting theorem
473:\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} used below.
474:
475:Fourier transformation of the sampled class-profile identities gives
476:\[
477: \Delta_\chi(y_i):=
478: \sum_{g\in E}\chi(g)
479: \bigl(\mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)-\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)\bigr)=0.
480:\]
481:For the trivial character this is already
482:\eqref{eq:elementary-two-group-base-determinant-equality}.  For non-trivial
483:\(\chi\), one has \(\chi^m=\chi\) for odd \(m\) and
484:\(\chi^m=\mathbf1\) for even \(m\).  The Adams--M\"obius calculation in
485:\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}, with the now common trivial
486:determinant coordinate, therefore gives
487:\[
488: \Delta_\chi(y)=\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H_\chi(y^{2^j}).
489:\]
490:
491:Choose an algebraic sampled radius \(y_0\).  If \(H_\chi\ne1\),
492:\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} supplies the unique normalized
493:\(R_\chi\in\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
494:\[
495: H_\chi(z)=\frac{R_\chi(z^2)}{R_\chi(z)^2},
496: \qquad R_\chi(y_0)=1.
497:\]
498:Write the reduced ratio \(H_\chi=P_{0,\chi}/P_{1,\chi}\) and put
499:\(D_\chi=\deg P_{0,\chi}+\deg P_{1,\chi}\).  Both character determinants
500:have degree at most \(V\), so \(D_\chi\le2V\).  By
501:\Cref{prop:logarithmic-mahler-divisor-bound} and the positive telescoping
502:identity in \Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate}, all real zeros of
503:\(\Delta_\chi\) lie among the non-zero roots of \(R_\chi-1\), of which there
504:are at most
505:\[
506: D_\chi\lceil\log_2(2D_\chi)\rceil-1
507: \le M(V)-1.
508:\]
509:The \(M(V)\) sampled zeros are therefore impossible.  Thus \(H_\chi=1\)
510:for every character \(\chi\).  The cross-base periodic-data dictionary in
511:\Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary}, followed by character Fourier inversion,
512:now gives equality of every primitive length--element count.
513:\end{proof}
514:
515:\begin{remark}[Located obstruction for general finite groups]
516:\label{rem:general-group-finite-sampling-interface}
517:For a same-base pair and \(\pi\in\Irr(G)\), put
518:\(H_\pi=P_{\pi,\tau}/P_{\pi,\tau'}\); then \(H_{\mathbf1}=1\).
519:Rearranging \eqref{eq:fixed-determinant-open-disc} by \(k=rm\) gives
520:\begin{equation}\label{eq:general-group-adams-mobius-obstruction}
521: \begin{aligned}
522: F_{\chi_\rho}^\tau(z)-F_{\chi_\rho}^{\tau'}(z)
523:   &=-\sum_{k\ge1}\frac1k\sum_{\pi\in\Irr(G)}
524:       b_{\rho,\pi}(k)\Log_0H_\pi(z^k),\\
525: b_{\rho,\pi}(k)
526:   &=\sum_{m\mid k}\mu(m)a_{\rho,\pi}^{(m)}.
527: \end{aligned}
528:\end{equation}
529:For \(C_2\), projection away from the common trivial channel makes these
530:coefficients vanish unless \(k\) is a power of two.  That lacunarity is exactly
531:what produces the scalar Mahler product in
532:\eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}.
533:
534:It already fails for \(C_3=\langle g\rangle\).  If \(\chi(g)=\omega\), record
535:the Adams states in the ordered basis
536:\((\mathbf1,\chi,\chi^2)\).  Their M\"obius transform is
537:\[
538: \mathbf b(k)=\sum_{m\mid k}\mu(m)e_{m\bmod3}.
539:\]
540:For a prime \(p\), this is zero when \(p\equiv1\pmod3\), equals
541:\(e_1-e_2\) when \(p\equiv2\pmod3\), and equals \(e_1-e_0\) when
542:\(p=3\).  There are infinitely many primes congruent to two modulo three:
543:if \(p_1,\ldots,p_r\) were all of them, any prime divisor congruent to two
544:modulo three of \(3p_1\cdots p_r-1\) would be new.  Thus
545:\eqref{eq:general-group-adams-mobius-obstruction} couples the two non-trivial
546:determinant ratios at infinitely many arithmetically distributed powers and
547:does not satisfy the scalar finite-degree Mahler equation used in
548:\Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting}.
549:
550:Accordingly the proof of a polynomial radial sampling bound for every finite
551:group stops here.  The missing input is a special-value theorem forcing
552:rationality from one algebraic common collision for this coupled cyclotomic
553:Euler system, together with an effective degree or zero bound for the resulting
554:certificate.  Neither the scalar lifting theorem nor the Pad\'e bound proved
555:above supplies that input.  The finite computation in
556:\Cref{sec:exactness} only checks the displayed \(C_3\) coefficients in a
557:finite range.
558:\end{remark}
559:
560:This mechanism is strictly weaker than full \(G\)-cospectrality, equivalently
561:represented cospectrality in every irreducible representation:
562:\eqref{eq:c2-collision-first-determinant} and
563:\eqref{eq:c2-collision-second-determinant} are different.  Represented
564:cospectrality in every irreducible representation instead requires equality
565:of the full twisted spectra and therefore preserves the complete periodic profile
566:\cite{BoyleSchmieding2017FiniteGroupExtensions,
567:CavaleriDonno2022Cospectrality}.
568:
569:Although one centered Perron-point vector loses information, an analytic radial profile
570:restores it.  The following is a sufficient recovery criterion; no optimality
571:claim about the amount of profile data is intended.
572:
573:\begin{theorem}[Radial-profile recovery]
574:\label{thm:radial-profile-recovery}
575:Let \(\tau:E(\Gamma)\to G\) and \(\tau':E(\Gamma')\to G\) be two
576:labellings over primitive base matrices with Perron roots
577:\(\lambda,\lambda'>1\); the bases need not agree.  Put
578:\(x=\min\{\lambda^{-1},(\lambda')^{-1}\}\).  For every conjugacy class \(C\),
579:define
580:\begin{equation}\label{eq:radial-profile-difference}
581: D_C(z):=\sum_{n\ge1}
582: \bigl(p_{n,C}(\tau)-p_{n,C}(\tau')\bigr)\log(1-z^n),
583:\end{equation}
584:where the logarithm is normalized at zero.  Every \(D_C\) is analytic on
585:\(|z|<x\).  If, for every \(C\), \(D_C\) vanishes on a set
586:\(S\subset\{|z|<x\}\) having an accumulation point in that disc,
587:then
588:\begin{equation}\label{eq:radial-profile-recovery}
589: p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')
590: \qquad(n\ge1,\ C\in\operatorname{Conj}(G)).
591:\end{equation}
592:It is enough, for example, to fix \(0<q<x\) and take
593:\(S=\{q^r:r\ge1\}\).
594:\end{theorem}
595:
596:\begin{proof}
597:Every primitive length-\(n\) orbit contributes \(n\) period-\(n\) points, so
598:\(np_{n,C}(\tau)\le\Tr(A^n)=O(\lambda^n)\), with the analogous bound
599:for \(\tau'\).  Since
600:\(-\log(1-z^n)=O(|z|^n)\) uniformly on compact subdiscs of
601:\(|z|<x\), \eqref{eq:radial-profile-difference} converges normally
602:there and defines an analytic function.
603:
604:If \(D_C\) vanishes on \(S\), the analytic identity theorem gives
605:\(D_C\equiv0\).  Suppose that \(n_0\) is the least length at which the two
606:primitive counts for this class differ.  In the expansion
607:\[
608: D_C(z)=-\sum_{n\ge1}\sum_{r\ge1}
609:  \frac{p_{n,C}(\tau)-p_{n,C}(\tau')}{r}z^{nr},
610:\]
611:every contribution to the coefficient of \(z^{n_0}\) from a proper divisor
612:of \(n_0\) vanishes by minimality.  That coefficient is therefore
613:\(-\bigl(p_{n_0,C}(\tau)-p_{n_0,C}(\tau')\bigr)\ne0\), a contradiction.
614:This proves \eqref{eq:radial-profile-recovery}.  Finally,
615:\(q^r<x\) for \(r\ge1\), and these points accumulate at zero inside the
616:disc.
617:\end{proof}
618:
619:For the collision in \Cref{thm:c2-boundary-collision},
620:\eqref{eq:c2-collision-exact-difference} equals \(2\log Q(z)\), and
621:\(Q(z)=1\) on \(0<z\le1/4\) only at \(z=1/4\).  Thus its centered equality
622:is an isolated Perron-boundary evaluation and cannot persist on any set allowed by
623:\Cref{thm:radial-profile-recovery}.

1:\subsection{Odd-Adams-invariant abelian two-group extensions}
2:\label{sec:odd-adams-sampling}
3:
4:The dyadic reduction extends beyond elementary two-groups precisely when the
5:odd Adams directions are constant.  We first record the two algebraic facts
6:needed for that extension.
7:
8:\begin{lemma}[Odd-Adams integrality and M\"obius collapse]
9:\label{lem:odd-adams-mobius-collapse}
10:Let \(G\) be a finite abelian \(2\)-group and let
11:\(\tau:E(\Gamma)\to G\) and \(\tau':E(\Gamma')\to G\) be one-step
12:cocycles.  For \(\chi\in\widehat G\), write
13:\[
14: P_{\chi,\tau}(z)=\det(I-zA_{\chi,\tau}),\qquad
15: P_{\chi,\tau'}(z)=\det(I-zA_{\chi,\tau'}),
16:\]
17:and assume, separately for the two cocycles, the condition denoted (OA):
18:\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-determinant-invariance}
19: \begin{aligned}
20: P_{\chi^u,\tau}(z)&=P_{\chi,\tau}(z),\\
21: P_{\chi^u,\tau'}(z)&=P_{\chi,\tau'}(z)
22: \end{aligned}
23: \qquad(\chi\in\widehat G,\ u\ \text{odd}).
24:\end{equation}
25:Then \(P_{\chi,\tau},P_{\chi,\tau'}\in\ZZ[z]\) for every \(\chi\).
26:If
27:\[
28: H_\chi(z):=\frac{P_{\chi,\tau}(z)}{P_{\chi,\tau'}(z)},\qquad
29: \Delta_\chi(z):=F_\chi^\tau(z)-F_\chi^{\tau'}(z),
30:\]
31:then, on the common open Perron disk,
32:\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-mobius-collapse}
33: \Delta_\chi(z)
34: =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\Log_0H_\chi(z^{2^j})
35:  +\sum_{j\ge1}2^{-j}\Log_0H_{\chi^2}(z^{2^j}).
36:\end{equation}
37:\end{lemma}
38:
39:\begin{proof}
40:Suppose that \(\chi\) has order \(2^a\), and put
41:\(K=\QQ(\chi(G))\).  The entries of \(A_{\chi,\tau}\) lie in the ring of
42:integers of \(K\), so the coefficients of \(P_{\chi,\tau}\) are algebraic
43:integers.  Every element of \(\operatorname{Gal}(K/\QQ)\) acts on the values
44:of \(\chi\) by \(\chi(g)\mapsto\chi(g)^u\) for some odd \(u\), and therefore
45:sends \(P_{\chi,\tau}\) to \(P_{\chi^u,\tau}\).  Condition
46:\eqref{eq:odd-adams-determinant-invariance} fixes this polynomial under the
47:whole Galois group.  Its coefficients are rational algebraic integers, hence
48:integers.  The same argument applies to \(\tau'\).
49:
50:For the collapse, the abelian specialization of
51:\eqref{eq:fixed-determinant-open-disc} gives the absolutely convergent identity
52:\begin{align}
53: \Delta_\chi(z)
54: &=-\sum_{r,m\ge1}\frac{\mu(m)}{rm}
55:      \Log_0H_{\chi^m}(z^{rm})\notag\\
56: &=-\sum_{k\ge1}\frac1k\sum_{m\mid k}\mu(m)
57:      \Log_0H_{\chi^m}(z^k).
58: \label{eq:odd-adams-collapse-before-divisors}
59:\end{align}
60:Write \(k=2^jq\), where \(q\) is odd.  The odd divisors contributing to the
61:inner sum have the form \(m=d\), \(d\mid q\), and
62:\[
63: \sum_{\substack{m\mid k\\m\ {\rm odd}}}\mu(m)
64: =\sum_{d\mid q}\mu(d)
65: =\begin{cases}1,&q=1,\\0,&q>1.\end{cases}
66:\]
67:If \(j\ge1\), the square-free even divisors are exactly \(m=2d\), with
68:\(d\mid q\) odd, and
69:\[
70: \sum_{\substack{m\mid k\\m\ {\rm even}}}\mu(m)
71: =\sum_{d\mid q}\mu(2d)
72: =-\sum_{d\mid q}\mu(d).
73:\]
74:For odd \(d\), condition (OA) gives
75:\[
76: H_{\chi^d}=H_\chi,\qquad
77: H_{\chi^{2d}}=H_{(\chi^2)^d}=H_{\chi^2}.
78:\]
79:Thus the inner divisor sum in
80:\eqref{eq:odd-adams-collapse-before-divisors} vanishes unless \(q=1\);
81:for \(k=1\) it is \(\Log_0H_\chi(z)\), and for \(k=2^j\), \(j\ge1\), it is
82:\[
83: \Log_0H_\chi(z^{2^j})-\Log_0H_{\chi^2}(z^{2^j}).
84:\]
85:Substitution proves \eqref{eq:odd-adams-mobius-collapse}.  This is an
86:identity of analytic germs, and hence throughout the common Perron disk.
87:\end{proof}
88:
89:\begin{theorem}[Odd-Adams-invariant finite radial determination]
90:\label{thm:odd-adams-abelian-two-group-finite-sampling}
91:Let \(G\) be a finite abelian \(2\)-group.  Let
92:\(\tau:E(\Gamma)\to G\) and \(\tau':E(\Gamma')\to G\) be one-step
93:cocycles over primitive non-negative integral base matrices \(A,A'\), whose
94:sizes are at most \(V\) and whose Perron roots are
95:\(\lambda,\lambda'>1\).  Assume that both cocycles satisfy (OA) in
96:\eqref{eq:odd-adams-determinant-invariance}.  Put
97:\[
98: x=\min\{\lambda^{-1},(\lambda')^{-1}\},\qquad
99: M(V)=2V\lceil\log_2(4V)\rceil.
100:\]
101:For \(g\in G\), define
102:\[
103: \mathcal E_g^\tau(y)
104: =\sum_{n\ge1}p_{n,g}(\tau)\log(1-y^n),\qquad 0<y<x,
105:\]
106:and define \(\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}\) analogously.  Suppose that
107:\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-sampled-profile-equality}
108: \mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)=\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)
109: \qquad(g\in G,\ 1\le i\le M(V))
110:\end{equation}
111:at \(M(V)\) distinct radii in \((0,x)\), at least one of which is algebraic.
112:Then
113:\[
114: p_{n,g}(\tau)=p_{n,g}(\tau')
115: \qquad(n\ge1,\ g\in G).
116:\]
117:The number \(M(V)\) of radial locations is independent of the rank and
118:exponent of \(G\), while the total number of scalar equalities in
119:\eqref{eq:odd-adams-sampled-profile-equality} is \(\abs G M(V)\).
120:Neither a common base nor a strict twisted spectral gap is required.
121:\end{theorem}
122:
123:\begin{proof}
124:All profile series converge absolutely on the stated interval by the
125:periodic-point estimate in \Cref{thm:finite-radial-sampling}.  Summing
126:\eqref{eq:odd-adams-sampled-profile-equality} over \(g\) gives
127:\[
128: \log\det(I-y_iA)=\log\det(I-y_iA')
129: \qquad(1\le i\le M(V)).
130:\]
131:The determinants are positive on \((0,x)\).  Their difference has degree at
132:most \(V\), vanishes at the sampled radii and at zero, and hence is zero:
133:\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-base-determinant-equality}
134: P_{\mathbf1,\tau}(z)=\det(I-zA)=\det(I-zA')
135: =P_{\mathbf1,\tau'}(z).
136:\end{equation}
137:Thus \(H_{\mathbf1}=1\).
138:
139:Fourier transformation of the sampled element-profile equalities gives
140:\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-sampled-fourier-equality}
141: \Delta_\chi(y_i)
142: =-\sum_{g\in G}\chi(g)
143:   \bigl(\mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)-\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)\bigr)
144: =0
145:\end{equation}
146:for every \(\chi\in\widehat G\) and every \(i\).  We prove
147:\(H_\chi=1\) by induction on the order of \(\chi\).  The order-one case is
148:\eqref{eq:odd-adams-base-determinant-equality}.  Assume the assertion for
149:all characters of order less than \(2^a\), and let \(\chi\) have order
150:\(2^a\).  Then \(H_{\chi^2}=1\), so
151:\Cref{lem:odd-adams-mobius-collapse} reduces to
152:\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-inductive-dyadic-orbit}
153: \Delta_\chi(y)
154: =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H_\chi(y^{2^j})
155: \qquad(0<y<x).
156:\end{equation}
157:
158:By \Cref{lem:odd-adams-mobius-collapse}, \(H_\chi\in\QQ(z)^\times\).
159:Entrywise,
160:\[
161: \abs{(A_{\chi,\tau})_{uv}}\le A_{uv},\qquad
162: \abs{(A_{\chi,\tau'})_{uv}}\le A'_{uv}.
163:\]
164:Perron-weighted domination therefore makes both character determinants
165:zero-free on their open Perron disks.  Since they are real polynomials with
166:value one at zero, they and \(H_\chi\) are positive on \((0,x)\).
167:
168:Choose an algebraic sampled radius \(y_0\).  Equations
169:\eqref{eq:odd-adams-sampled-fourier-equality} and
170:\eqref{eq:odd-adams-inductive-dyadic-orbit} give
171:\[
172: \prod_{j\ge0}H_\chi(y_0^{2^j})^{2^{-j}}=1.
173:\]
174:If \(H_\chi\ne1\), \Cref{thm:general-rational-p-mahler-lifting} with \(p=2\)
175:gives the unique normalized \(R_\chi\in\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
176:\[
177: H_\chi(z)=\frac{R_\chi(z^2)}{R_\chi(z)^2},\qquad R_\chi(y_0)=1.
178:\]
179:Write \(H_\chi=P_{0,\chi}/P_{1,\chi}\) in reduced form and put
180:\(D_\chi=\deg P_{0,\chi}+\deg P_{1,\chi}\).  Both determinants have degree
181:at most \(V\), so \(D_\chi\le2V\).  The rational telescope and
182:\Cref{prop:logarithmic-mahler-divisor-bound} show that every real zero of
183:\(\Delta_\chi\) is a non-zero root of \(R_\chi-1\), and that there are at
184:most
185:\[
186: b_2(D_\chi)-1
187: =D_\chi\lceil\log_2(2D_\chi)\rceil-1
188: \le M(V)-1
189:\]
190:such roots.  This contradicts the \(M(V)\) distinct zeros in
191:\eqref{eq:odd-adams-sampled-fourier-equality}.  Hence \(H_\chi=1\), closing
192:the induction.
193:
194:All character determinants now agree between the two systems.  The
195:cross-base periodic-data dictionary in \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary},
196:followed by Fourier inversion on \(G\), recovers every
197:\(p_{n,g}\), as asserted.
198:\end{proof}
199:
200:\begin{remark}[Concrete scope of (OA)]
201:\label{rem:odd-adams-concrete-scope}
202:Condition (OA) is automatic for \(G=(C_2)^r\).  A stronger entrywise
203:sufficient condition for a general abelian \(2\)-group is that, for every
204:ordered vertex pair, every \(g\in G\), and every odd \(u\), the number of
205:\(g\)-labelled edges equals the number of \(g^u\)-labelled edges.  It then
206:gives \(A_{\chi^u}=A_\chi\), not merely equality of their determinants.
207:
208:For \(C_4=\langle a\rangle\), this condition says exactly that the
209:\(a\)- and \(a^{-1}\)-labelled edge counts agree entrywise; the \(e\)- and
210:\(a^2\)-counts are unrestricted.  It does not force factorization through
211:\(C_2\): a one-vertex graph with equally many \(a\)- and \(a^{-1}\)-loops
212:has primitive base and holonomy subgroup \(C_4\).  Likewise, assigning equal
213:counts on each odd-power orbit in \(C_{2^s}\) gives examples with genuine
214:holonomy of order \(2^s\).
215:\end{remark}

233:\begin{theorem}[Conditional prime-primary collision--jet rigidity]
234:\label{thm:prime-primary-collision-jet-rigidity}
235:Let \(\ell\) be prime and let \(G\) be a finite abelian \(\ell\)-group.
236:Let \(\tau,\tau'\) be one-step \(G\)-cocycles over primitive non-negative
237:integral base matrices \(A,A'\), of sizes \(v,v'\), with Perron roots
238:\(\lambda,\lambda'>1\).  Put
239:\[
240: x=\min\{\lambda^{-1},(\lambda')^{-1}\},
241:\]
242:and assume relative unit-Adams invariance
243:\eqref{eq:relative-unit-adams}.  Suppose that, for integers \(L\ge0\) and
244:\(K\ge1\),
245:\begin{align}
246: p_{n,g}(\tau)&=p_{n,g}(\tau')
247: &&(1\le n\le L,\ g\in G),
248: \label{eq:prime-primary-initial-jet}\\
249: \mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)&=\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)
250: &&(g\in G,\ 1\le i\le K),
251: \label{eq:prime-primary-profile-samples}
252:\end{align}
253:at distinct radii \(0<y_i<x\), at least one of which is algebraic.  Assume
254:also the following statement, denoted \textup{(KN85)} and attributed to
255:Keiji Nishioka's 1985 paper, whose bibliographic record is verified but whose
256:original printed statement has not been verified:
257:\begin{quote}
258:For every integer \(p\ge2\) and every \(H\in\CC(z)^\times\), every
259:convergent Laurent-series germ \(F\in\CC((z))\) that is algebraic over
260:\(\CC(z)\) and satisfies
261:\begin{equation}\label{eq:kn85-explicit-assumption}
262: F(z^p)=\frac{F(z)^p}{H(z)}
263:\end{equation}
264:belongs to \(\CC(z)\),
265:\end{quote}
266:If
267:\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-cross-base-threshold}
268: K+L\ge\max\{v,v'\},
269:\end{equation}
270:then
271:\[
272: p_{n,g}(\tau)=p_{n,g}(\tau')
273: \qquad(n\ge1,\ g\in G).
274:\]
275:If the base determinants are already equal, it is enough to assume
276:\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-fixed-determinant-threshold}
277: K+L\ge
278: \left\lfloor\frac{v+v'}{2(\ell-1)}\right\rfloor.
279:\end{equation}
280:\end{theorem}
281:
282:\begin{proof}
283:Summing \eqref{eq:prime-primary-profile-samples} over \(g\) gives
284:\[
285: \log\det(I-y_iA)=\log\det(I-y_iA')
286: \qquad(1\le i\le K).
287:\]
288:Both determinants are positive on \((0,x)\), so their values agree at the
289:\(y_i\).  Likewise, summing \eqref{eq:prime-primary-initial-jet} over \(g\)
290:and using the primitive-orbit product gives
291:\[
292: \det(I-zA)-\det(I-zA')=O(z^{L+1}).
293:\]
294:The polynomial on the left has degree at most \(\max\{v,v'\}\).  Under
295:\eqref{eq:prime-primary-cross-base-threshold}, its zero of multiplicity at
296:least \(L+1\) at zero and its \(K\) distinct positive zeros force it to
297:vanish identically.  Thus in either case under consideration the base
298:determinants agree and
299:\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-trivial-ratio}
300: H_{\mathbf1}=1.
301:\end{equation}
302:
303:Fourier transformation of \eqref{eq:prime-primary-profile-samples} gives
304:\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-fourier-samples}
305: \Delta_\chi(y_i)=0
306: \qquad(\chi\in\widehat G,\ 1\le i\le K).
307:\end{equation}
308:We prove \(H_\chi=1\) by induction on the order of \(\chi\).  The trivial
309:case is \eqref{eq:prime-primary-trivial-ratio}.  Let \(\chi\) have order
310:\(\ell^a\) and suppose that all lower-order character ratios are one.  Then
311:\(H_{\chi^\ell}=1\), and
312:\Cref{lem:prime-primary-adams-collapse} reduces to
313:\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-one-orbit}
314: \Delta_\chi(z)
315: =-\sum_{j\ge0}\ell^{-j}\Log_0H_\chi(z^{\ell^j}).
316:\end{equation}
317:
318:By \Cref{lem:prime-primary-adams-collapse}, \(H_\chi\in\QQ(z)\).  The
319:Perron-weighted domination in \Cref{lem:perron-weighted-domination} makes its
320:numerator and denominator zero-free on \(\abs z<x\).  Since
321:\(H_\chi(0)=1\) and \(H_\chi\) is real, it is positive on \((0,x)\).
322:Choose an algebraic sampled radius \(y_0\).  If \(H_\chi\ne1\), then
323:\eqref{eq:prime-primary-fourier-samples} and
324:\eqref{eq:prime-primary-one-orbit} give
325:\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-algebraic-product}
326: \prod_{j\ge0}H_\chi(y_0^{\ell^j})^{\ell^{-j}}=1.
327:\end{equation}
328:Define the convergent germ
329:\[
330: F_\chi(z)=\prod_{j\ge0}H_\chi(z^{\ell^j})^{\ell^{-j}}.
331:\]
332:It belongs to \(1+z\QQ[[z]]\) and satisfies
333:\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-critical-equation}
334: F_\chi(z^\ell)=\frac{F_\chi(z)^\ell}{H_\chi(z)}.
335:\end{equation}
336:The proof of \Cref{thm:general-rational-p-mahler-lifting}, through its
337:application of Kumiko Nishioka's 1982 theorem, applies verbatim: one has
338:\(0<y_0<x<1\), a radius \(r\in(y_0,x)\) gives the required zero- and
339:pole-free disk, and that proof establishes the coefficient-height and
340:common-denominator bounds for every rational input.  Hence
341:\eqref{eq:prime-primary-algebraic-product}, which says \(F_\chi(y_0)=1\),
342:forces \(F_\chi\) to be algebraic over \(\CC(z)\).  Assumption
343:\textup{(KN85)} applied to \eqref{eq:prime-primary-critical-equation} now
344:gives \(F_\chi\in\CC(z)\).  Since its Taylor coefficients are rational,
345:coefficientwise Galois invariance gives \(F_\chi\in\QQ(z)\).  Therefore
346:\(R_\chi=F_\chi^{-1}\) is the unique normalized element of
347:\(\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
348:\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-rational-certificate}
349: H_\chi(z)=\frac{R_\chi(z^\ell)}{R_\chi(z)^\ell},
350: \qquad R_\chi(y_0)=1.
351:\end{equation}
352:The positive product defining the lift also shows that
353:\(R_\chi(t)>0\) for \(0\le t<x\).
354:
355:Substitution of \eqref{eq:prime-primary-rational-certificate} into
356:\eqref{eq:prime-primary-one-orbit} telescopes to
357:\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-rational-telescope}
358: \Delta_\chi(z)=\ell\log R_\chi(z).
359:\end{equation}
360:Thus \eqref{eq:prime-primary-fourier-samples} gives
361:\(R_\chi(y_i)=1\) for every \(i\).  Moreover,
362:\eqref{eq:prime-primary-initial-jet} gives
363:\(\Delta_\chi(z)=O(z^{L+1})\), so
364:\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-certificate-jet}
365: \nu_\chi:=\operatorname{ord}_{z=0}(R_\chi(z)-1)\ge L+1.
366:\end{equation}
367:
368:Write \(H_\chi=P_{0,\chi}/P_{1,\chi}\) in reduced form and put
369:\(D_\chi=\deg P_{0,\chi}+\deg P_{1,\chi}\).  Cancellation from the two
370:original determinants can only lower degrees, hence
371:\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-input-degree}
372: D_\chi\le v+v'.
373:\end{equation}
374:Applying \Cref{thm:collision-jet-inequality} to
375:\eqref{eq:prime-primary-rational-certificate} gives
376:\begin{equation}\label{eq:prime-primary-final-count}
377: K+L+1\le K+\nu_\chi
378: \le\rho(R_\chi)
379: \le\left\lfloor\frac{D_\chi}{2(\ell-1)}\right\rfloor.
380:\end{equation}
381:The last member is at most \(\max\{v,v'\}\), contradicting
382:\eqref{eq:prime-primary-cross-base-threshold}; when the base determinants were
383:known in advance, \eqref{eq:prime-primary-input-degree} instead makes
384:\eqref{eq:prime-primary-final-count} contradict
385:\eqref{eq:prime-primary-fixed-determinant-threshold}.  Therefore
386:\(H_\chi=1\), closing the induction.
387:
388:All character determinants now agree.  The comparison dictionary in
389:\Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary}, followed by Fourier inversion on \(G\),
390:recovers every primitive length--element count.
391:\end{proof}
392:
393:\begin{corollary}[Conditional linear radial determination]
394:\label{cor:prime-primary-linear-radial-determination}
395:Assume \textup{(KN85)}: for every \(p\ge2\) and
396:\(H\in\CC(z)^\times\), every convergent Laurent-series germ
397:\(F\in\CC((z))\) algebraic over \(\CC(z)\) and satisfying
398:\(F(z^p)=F(z)^p/H(z)\) belongs to \(\CC(z)\).  Under the remaining
399:hypotheses of \Cref{thm:prime-primary-collision-jet-rigidity}, with \(L=0\),
400:\(\max\{v,v'\}\) full profile vectors, one algebraically anchored, determine
401:all primitive length--element data.  In particular, \(V\) radial locations
402:suffice for bases of size at most \(V\).
403:\end{corollary}
404:
405:\begin{corollary}[Conditional binary linear sampling bound]
406:\label{cor:exact-binary-radial-sampling-order}
407:Assume \textup{(KN85)}: for every \(p\ge2\) and
408:\(H\in\CC(z)^\times\), every convergent Laurent-series germ
409:\(F\in\CC((z))\) algebraic over \(\CC(z)\) and satisfying

11:The bases need not coincide.  The theorem contains the elementary
12:\((C_2)^r\) result and covers standard extensions with genuine higher
13:two-power holonomy.  A
14:strict twisted gap permits centered, not raw, class profiles at a Perron
15:endpoint in the binary scalar theorem.  The determinant ratio governing the
16:test is canonically the ratio of the standard Artin--Mazur zeta functions of

18:produces a unique rational Mahler certificate.  For every fixed \(p\ge2\),
19:the total-degree estimate bounds the numerator-plus-denominator degree

24:system is rational reconstruction under the resulting cap.  The exact four-vertex

26:invariant; every corresponding raw class profile diverges to \(-\infty\).

28:base has \(m\) distinct rational collisions but different periodic data,
29:giving the unconditional lower bound

54:still uses the strict gap only to continue through the Perron circle.

57:Conditional on \textup{(KN85)}, the prime-primary collapse reduces each

59:same mechanism does not presently
60:yield a polynomial sample

62:two character determinants at infinitely many arithmetically distributed

84:conditional on \textup{(KN85)}.

21:## Abstract
22:
23:Let G be a finite abelian 2-group, and assume that the twisted determinants
24:of two one-step G-cocycles are invariant under every odd Adams operation.
25:The cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts whose vertex counts are at most
26:V; the bases need not be the same. For the primitive length-element counts
27:p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1) p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap
28:hypothesis, equality of every element profile at
29:2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron interval forces
30:equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius is algebraic.
31:The number of radial locations is independent of the rank and exponent of G.
32:The hypothesis is automatic for G=(C2)^r and permits genuine holonomy of
33:orders 4, 8, and beyond. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: a parity-free
34:rational critical p-Mahler construction combines an elementary
35:linear-exponent denominator estimate with Kumiko Nishioka's verified
36:special-value theorem. The algebraic-to-rational implication attributed to
37:Keiji Nishioka is isolated as the unverified assumption (KN85) in the
38:conditional linear theorem. Determinant parity gives a stronger integral
39:refinement. For the multiplicative certificate itself, an input-only
40:divisor estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound in terms of the reduced
41:input degree alone. Its order is sharp abstractly and on standard realizable
42:C2-cover zeta ratios. Explicit height and fixed-p bit bounds are supporting
43:quantitative consequences; the Pade step is rational reconstruction after a
44:degree cap is known. A second standard-cover family gives m exact rational collisions on
45:4m+2 vertices and hence an Omega(V) sampling lower bound. For general finite
46:groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation point;
47:already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a finite
48:bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.
49:
50:The manuscript also gives an unconditional sharp squarefree Mahler bound, a
51:collision--jet inequality, and odd-prime collision families with delayed
52:first discrepancy. The stronger prime-primary linear theorem and the binary
53:linear upper bound are conditional on the explicitly quoted assumption
54:(KN85); they are not the headline and do not close the sampling order
55:unconditionally.
56:
57:Keywords: one-sided edge shift; finite-group extension; inverse problem;
58:Mahler function; twisted determinant; Adams operation; primitive orbit;
59:finite sampling

81:## Venue and paper architecture
82:
83:ETDS remains a defensible ambitious submission because the principal result
84:is the dynamical inverse theorem: finite radial determination of represented
85:periodic data for odd-Adams-invariant finite abelian two-group extensions,
86:with cross-base recovery, rank- and exponent-independent radial depth, exact
87:collisions, and realizable lower bounds. This is a central dynamical problem
88:at the interface with number theory and combinatorics. The Mahler theorem is a
89:strong supporting theorem that improves the paper's completeness and
90:effectivity; it does not carry the journal-tier case.
91:
92:A symbolic-computation venue is not a better home for the present whole
93:paper, whose headline and standard conclusion are dynamical. A focused
94:functional-equations extraction was considered, but splitting was declined:
95:the quantitative Mahler result is more meaningful here because its sharpness
96:is realized by standard C2-cover zeta ratios, while the dynamics paper uses
97:the result as its effective arithmetic engine.

109:## Priority boundary
110:
111:Ostrowski (1968) treats the linear multiplicative equation. Kumiko Nishioka's
112:1982 special-value statement was checked directly. Keiji Nishioka's 1985
113:bibliographic record is verified, but the original theorem statement is not:
114:the pages are paywalled and the zbMATH review is only a secondary restatement.
115:The precise algebraic-to-rational implication needed for the conditional
116:linear theorem is quoted as assumption `(KN85)`. The
117:claimed contribution is limited to parity-compatible algebraic collision
118:lifting in the dynamical setting, the input-only multiplicative-certificate
119:divisor estimate and its sharp lower-bound family, the supporting height and
120:fixed-p bit estimates, the cross-base odd-Adams-invariant abelian 2-group
121:theorem, the unconditional squarefree and collision--jet estimates, and the
122:realizable collision families. No priority claim is made from the antecedent
123:search.

1:# Finite radial determination for abelian two-group SFT extensions
2:
3:This directory builds two related papers.
4:
5:- `main.tex` is the inverse-theorem manuscript. Its spine is finite radial
6:  determination for odd-Adams-invariant extensions by arbitrary finite
7:  abelian 2-groups over possibly different bases, without a twisted-gap
8:  hypothesis in the open Perron interval. It also contains the parity-free
9:  rational critical Mahler lifting theorem, a sharp input-only divisor bound
10:  for its multiplicative certificate, and realizable lower-bound families on
11:  standard `C2` covers. It also proves an unconditional sharp squarefree
12:  divisor bound, a collision--jet inequality, and odd-prime collision
13:  constructions. The stronger prime-primary linear theorem is stated
14:  conditionally on the explicit assumption `(KN85)` because the original
15:  Keiji Nishioka 1985 statement has not been verified.
16:- `supplement.tex` contains the Adams-corrected Frobenius-class product
17:  constant, quotient-cover refinements, and the exact strict-gap `S3`
18:  witness. These results are logically separate from the inverse theorem.
19:
20:For base matrices of size at most `V`, the proved uniform sampling budget is
21:
22:```text
23:M(V) = 2 V ceil(log2(4V)).
24:```
25:
26:The radii lie in the common open Perron interval and at least one is
27:algebraic. A strict twisted gap is required only for the binary endpoint
28:extension. The theorem is automatic for elementary 2-groups and covers
29:genuine higher 2-power holonomy under odd-Adams invariance. A standard-cover
30:family gives an `Omega(V)` sampling lower bound, while a separate realizable
31:family shows that the `O(D log D)` Mahler certificate-degree bound has the
32:correct order.
33:
34:No finite polynomial sampling bound is claimed for every finite group. The
35:paper locates the obstruction already at `C3`: Adams--Mobius inversion has
36:non-lacunary support and produces a coupled cyclotomic Euler system for which
37:the required special-value and effective zero theorems are not available.
38:

1:\section{Conclusion}
2:\label{sec:conclusion}
3:
4:For odd-Adams-invariant extensions by any finite abelian \(2\)-group \(G\)
5:over two primitive bases of at most \(V\) vertices,
6:\(2V\lceil\log_2(4V)\rceil\) radial locations in the common open Perron
7:interval determine the complete primitive length--element profile, provided
8:that one location is algebraic.  This radial depth is independent of the rank
9:and exponent of \(G\), but each location supplies a full
10:\(\abs G\)-component vector, for \(\abs G M(V)\) scalar comparisons in total.
11:The bases need not coincide.  The theorem contains the elementary
12:\((C_2)^r\) result and covers standard extensions with genuine higher
13:two-power holonomy.  A
14:strict twisted gap permits centered, not raw, class profiles at a Perron
15:endpoint in the binary scalar theorem.  The determinant ratio governing the
16:test is canonically the ratio of the standard Artin--Mazur zeta functions of
17:the two binary covers.  The proof is effective: one algebraic collision
18:produces a unique rational Mahler certificate.  For every fixed \(p\ge2\),
19:the total-degree estimate bounds the numerator-plus-denominator degree
20:of this multiplicative certificate, from the reduced input degree alone, by
21:\(b_p(D)=O_p(D\log D)\).  Its order is sharp abstractly and on realizable
22:standard \(C_2\)-cover zeta ratios.  The explicit height and fixed-\(p\) bit
23:complexity estimates are useful further consequences; the finite Pad\'e
24:system is rational reconstruction under the resulting cap.  The exact four-vertex
25:pair shows why a single centered Perron-boundary vector cannot be an inverse
26:invariant; every corresponding raw class profile diverges to \(-\infty\).
27:For every \(m\), an explicit binary pair on a common \(4m+2\)-vertex positive
28:base has \(m\) distinct rational collisions but different periodic data,
29:giving the unconditional lower bound
30:\(\mathsf N_{C_2}(V)\ge\lfloor(V-2)/4\rfloor+1\).
31:For each odd prime \(\ell\), a pair on \(\ell(2m+1)\) vertices has \(m\)
32:rational collisions, agrees through length \(m\), and first differs at length
33:\(m+1\) by an explicit element vector.
34:The squarefree estimate
35:\(2(p-1)\deg\rad(AB)\le D\), the collision--jet inequality, and these
36:odd-prime constructions are unconditional.  Subject to the explicitly
37:quoted assumption \textup{(KN85)}, they also give the stronger linear
38:prime-primary theorem and the upper bound \(\mathsf N_{C_2}(V)\le V\).
39:
40:The determinant lifting theorem is a specialization of a parity-free rational
41:critical \(p\)-Mahler statement.  Its coefficient recursion gives the exact
42:bound
43:\[
44: (pq)^{2n-1}f_n\in\ZZ,\qquad
45: \log d_h\le(2h-1)\log(pq),
46:\]
47:which is sufficient for Kumiko Nishioka's verified 1982 special-value
48:theorem.  The next algebraic-to-rational implication is precisely
49:\textup{(KN85)}.  Keiji Nishioka's 1985 bibliographic record is verified, but
50:the original statement is not; the conditional theorem therefore includes
51:the required implication in its hypotheses.  Determinant parity is a convenient strong
52:sufficient condition yielding integral coefficients through
53:Dieudonn\'e--Dwork, not an essential lifting hypothesis.  The endpoint form
54:still uses the strict gap only to continue through the Perron circle.
55:
56:The full dyadic Adams--M\"obius collapse proves the headline theorem.
57:Conditional on \textup{(KN85)}, the prime-primary collapse reduces each
58:relatively unit-Adams-invariant channel to one \(\ell\)-Mahler orbit.  The
59:same mechanism does not presently
60:yield a polynomial sample
61:bound for every finite group.  For \(C_3\), Adams--M\"obius inversion already couples
62:two character determinants at infinitely many arithmetically distributed
63:powers, rather than one lacunary Mahler orbit.  A general finite-group theorem
64:therefore requires a new special-value and effective zero theory for these
65:coupled Euler systems.  Generic \(C_4\) outside the relative unit-Adams-invariant
66:subclass has the analogous coupled obstruction.  In its absence, the proved
67:general statement remains unconditional analytic recovery from a profile set
68:with an interior accumulation point.
69:
70:The novelty claim is correspondingly narrow.  No priority claim is made for
71:either Nishioka interface or from the antecedent search.
72:Frobenius-class Euler products, their character expansion,
73:algebraic-solution rationality for rational functional equations, and the
74:general periodic-data dictionary are cited background.  The original Mahler
75:increment is the input-only \(b_p(D)\) divisor estimate for the multiplicative
76:certificate, its \(\Omega_p(D\log D)\) family, and the transfer of that
77:sharpness to realizable \(C_2\)-cover zeta ratios.  The height bound and fixed-
78:\(p\) integer bit complexity are useful but incremental.  Bare existence and
79:decidability reduce, by logarithmic differentiation, to the published
80:additive and linear Mahler algorithms; Pad\'e reconstruction is largely
81:standard after a degree cap is known.  The central result remains the
82:cross-base odd-Adams-invariant abelian two-group inverse theorem with the
83:\(O(V\log V)\) radial budget.  The prime-primary linear strengthening is
84:conditional on \textup{(KN85)}.
85:
86:The principal dynamical theorem remains an inverse theorem for the
87:paper-specific sampled fixed-label Euler values.  Its standard dynamical
88:conclusion is represented periodic-data equivalence, via the cited
89:determinant/periodic-data dictionary.  It does not advance conjugacy, strong
90:shift equivalence, cocycle cohomology, switching, Bowen--Franks or flow

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible â†’ gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI â†’ build â†’ signing, API â†’ service â†’ database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets â†’ workflow âœ“, workflow â†’ build âœ—)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes â†’ Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If â‰¥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultrathink this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms â‰  understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

**Related skills:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - For creating failing test case (Phase 4, Step 1)
- **superpowers:verification-before-completion** - Verify fix worked before claiming success

## Real-World Impact

From debugging sessions:
- Systematic approach: 15-30 minutes to fix
- Random fixes approach: 2-3 hours of thrashing
- First-time fix rate: 95% vs 40%
- New bugs introduced: Near zero vs common

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the artifact tests and archive a timing-free LF transcript."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


MODULES = (
    "artifacts.test_verify_a5_results",
    "artifacts.test_verify_linear_collision_claims",
    "artifacts.test_verify_twisted_determinant_rigidity",
)


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output",
        type=Path,
        default=Path(__file__).with_name("unittest_output.txt"),
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    display_command = "python -m unittest -v " + " ".join(MODULES)
    command = [sys.executable, "-m", "unittest", "-v", *MODULES]
    completed = subprocess.run(
        command,
        cwd=root,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )
    transcript = completed.stdout + completed.stderr
    print(transcript, end="")
    stable_transcript = re.sub(
        r"^(Ran \d+ tests?) in [0-9.]+s$",
        r"\1",
        transcript.replace("\r\n", "\n"),
        flags=re.MULTILINE,
    )
    archive = (
        f"Python version: {sys.version.split()[0]}\n"
        f"command: {display_command}\n"
        "random seed: none (deterministic)\n\n"
        + stable_transcript
    )
    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.output.write_text(archive, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    return completed.returncode


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

89:\begin{theorem}[Odd-Adams-invariant finite radial determination]
90:\label{thm:odd-adams-abelian-two-group-finite-sampling}
91:Assume \textup{(KN85)}: for every integer \(q\ge2\) and every
92:\(J\in\CC(z)^\times\), every convergent Laurent-series germ
93:\(f\in\CC((z))\) algebraic over \(\CC(z)\) and satisfying
94:\(f(z^q)=f(z)^q/J(z)\) belongs to \(\CC(z)\).
95:Let \(G\) be a finite abelian \(2\)-group.  Let
96:\(\tau:E(\Gamma)\to G\) and \(\tau':E(\Gamma')\to G\) be one-step
97:cocycles over primitive non-negative integral base matrices \(A,A'\), whose
98:sizes are at most \(V\) and whose Perron roots are
99:\(\lambda,\lambda'>1\).  Assume that both cocycles satisfy (OA) in
100:\eqref{eq:odd-adams-determinant-invariance}.  Put
101:\[
102: x=\min\{\lambda^{-1},(\lambda')^{-1}\},\qquad
103: M(V)=2V\lceil\log_2(4V)\rceil.
104:\]
105:For \(g\in G\), define
106:\[
107: \mathcal E_g^\tau(y)
108: =\sum_{n\ge1}p_{n,g}(\tau)\log(1-y^n),\qquad 0<y<x,
109:\]
110:and define \(\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}\) analogously.  Suppose that
111:\begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-adams-sampled-profile-equality}
112: \mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)=\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)
113: \qquad(g\in G,\ 1\le i\le M(V))
114:\end{equation}
115:at \(M(V)\) distinct radii in \((0,x)\), at least one of which is algebraic.
116:Then
117:\[
118: p_{n,g}(\tau)=p_{n,g}(\tau')
119: \qquad(n\ge1,\ g\in G).
120:\]
121:The number \(M(V)\) of radial locations is independent of the rank and
122:exponent of \(G\), while the total number of scalar equalities in
123:\eqref{eq:odd-adams-sampled-profile-equality} is \(\abs G M(V)\).
124:Neither a common base nor a strict twisted spectral gap is required.
125:\end{theorem}
